newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-PUMAS CONTINUE SUCCESSFUL TOUR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PUMAS CONTINUE SUCCESSFUL TOUR.

text.p: The Argentine Pumas continued their impressive tour of England with a 10-try, 64-14 rout of the Northern Counties on Sunday, taking their points tally in just four matches to 242.
England's next opposition - Argentina take them on at Twickenham on December 14 - brushed aside a woefully inadequate North side made up largely of players from division two clubs.

The North were handed some salutary lessons from the rampant tourists. Argentina's giant pack, with a huge per-man advantage, steamrollered their lightweight counterparts into submission, with massive Milan lock German Llanes providing a reminder of the line-out havoc he wreaked against England in last year's World Cup.

Exciting fly-half Jose Cilley and penetrative centre Eduardo Simone made the most of plentiful possession and speedy wingers Facundo Soler and Tomas Solari took advantage to race over for a brace of tries apiece.
Number eight Pablo Bouza also scored two tries and Cilley demonstrated wonderful place kicking with seven conversions from 10 attempts.
The outclassed North at least showed bags of spirit and they trailed only 38-16 in the second half after stand-off John Stabler kicked his fourth goal from as many attempts.
Right winger Gary Monighan had earlier breached the Pumas' tryline when he won the race to his own kick-ahead for a nice try.
